question.text: Compared to a typical mutual fund, a Cat III AIF following a Long-Short Strategy differs PRIMARILY because:

answer.text: MF can run 130/30 freely; Cat III cannot short.
Cat III permits short selling and 2x leverage, while MFs have far more restrictive short and leverage rules.
Cat III is open to retail; MF is HNI-only.
Both are identically regulated under SEBI (MF) Regulations.

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Cat III's defining regulatory feature: can go SHORT and can use 2x leverage — MFs (ex the narrow specified offerings) have very limited shorting and no active leverage. This is why hedge strategies live in Cat III AIF, not in MF. **The Trap:** A inverts. C inverts investor eligibility. D is wrong — MF Regulations and AIF Regulations are separate. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-B (Cat III Distributor) tests same. XXI-B (PMS) is yet another regime. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** The retail pitch 'we are like an MF but can short' is technically right but regulatorily sensitive; PPM should stress 'accredited investor / INR 1 cr minimum' at every touch. Distributor (XIX-B) onboarding compliance catches loose language.
